newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Surprise crude draw possible in APIs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Surprise crude draw possible in APIs.

text.p: Many traders expect Tuesday's oil inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) to show a build in crude stocks, but others suspect imports may have subsided while refinery runs increased resulting in a surprise draw in stocks.
"Imports have probably backed off a bit, while West Coast stocks are due to correct after a large build last week," said John Saucer, analyst with Smith Barney in Houston.
Most of the 6.4 million barrel crude build in last week's data was due to a five million barrel build in the West Coast.
A consensus of trader estimates gathered by Reuters forecasts crude stocks to build one million barrels in Tuesday's data which reflects the week ended April 4.
The estimates ranged from a build of three million barrels to a draw of three million barrels. Estimates by those expecting a draw averaged a fall of two million barrels.

The argument for rising crude stocks is based on a belief that imports from the North Sea and West Africa continue at a strong pace. Some are calling for total imports to rise above the eight million barrel per day (bpd) milestone after rising by 827,000 bpd to 7.7 million bpd for the week ended March 28.
"The focus of the APIs are the imports. If imports go above eight million barrels a day that could be seen as a big deal, and very bearish," said a New York crude trader.
Indeed, prompt crude fell almost $1.75 a barrel last week on views of a growing crude stock surplus.
But, some noted the historical bias is towards a draw in crude stocks in the first week in April.

"Seasonally speaking crude draws in early April have depended one how fast refineries come out of turnaround, and crude runs have been increasing steadily," said William Brown, president of New York trading firm W.H. Brown & Co.
Due to several mishaps suffered by refineries last week, including a fire at Exxon's Baton Rouge, La. refinery, traders expect refinery runs to have dropped 0.50 percentage point.
But, last week's data showed refinery operations already running 1.5 percentage points above a year ago.

Moreover, some traders said emergence of refineries from winter turnaround will offset the loss in operating rates from the mishaps, pushing up the weekly run rate. Meanwhile, a rise in implied gasoline demand from the lacklustre 7.4 million bpd seen in last week's data is expected push gasoline stocks down between one and two and a half million barrels.

Distillate stocks, comprised of heating oil and diesel, are expected to follow their seasonal trend of declines as refiners focus on gasoline production ahead of the summer driving season. Traders expected distillate stocks to drop up to two and a half million barrels.
